section_summary: This section follows the growth of Japanese trade unions after surrender and American occupation policy toward labor organization, disputes, and police conduct. It includes a legal analysis of workers’ temporary control of businesses, translations of police instructions and the 1946 Labor Relations Adjustment Law, and correspondence urging stronger labor administration. The final pages begin a survey of Japanese writing on unions, wages, strikes, and unemployment.

subfiles.title: Revival of the Free Working Organization
subfiles.about: The article describes the suppression and postwar revival of Japanese trade unions.
subfiles.summary: It contrasts government-aligned labor bodies with independent unions and argues that free mass unions are necessary for Japanese democracy.

subfiles.title: Meetings with Members of Labor Commission to Japan
subfiles.about: State Department officers briefed visiting labor commissioners on Japanese labor issues.
subfiles.summary: The commission discussed labor legislation, occupation policy, and a projected World Federation of Trade Unions visit. Sullivan expected further labor materials from its members.

subfiles.title: Ministerial Control of Labor Affairs in Japan
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department requests an assessment of conflicting reports about Japanese control of labor affairs.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a January 31 memorandum and seeks the political adviser’s judgment before approaching SCAP.

subfiles.title: Draft instruction on ministerial control of labor affairs
subfiles.about: An earlier draft requests judgment on Japanese ministerial plans for labor affairs.
subfiles.summary: Drafts the request later issued as instruction No. 96.

subfiles.title: Suggested Legal Justifications for Labor’s Assertion of Managerial Powers in Japanese Labor Disputes
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, United States Political Adviser’s office
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a memorandum on the legality of workers’ temporary control of businesses.
subfiles.summary: Introduces Suehiro Izutarō’s controversial legal defense of managerial control in labor disputes.

subfiles.title: Suggested Legal Justifications of Labor’s Assertion of Managerial Powers in Japanese Labor Disputes
subfiles.about: The memorandum examines legal arguments for workers’ temporary exercise of management powers.
subfiles.summary: It reviews disputes at a coal mine, Yomiuri-Hochi, and Keisei Electric Railroad and the Japanese government’s warning against infringements of ownership. It explains Suehiro’s argument that temporary, nonviolent worker control can be a lawful bargaining measure under the Labor Union Law, while permanent participation requires owners’ consent. The memorandum notes the tension between new labor rights and older property concepts.

subfiles.title: The Legality and the Limitations of Labor’s Exercise of Management Controls
subfiles.about: Suehiro argues for the legality of temporary worker control during labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: He distinguishes lawful dispute tactics from criminal acts and permanent management rights. He argues that temporary control may be less harmful than a lawful strike, while enduring worker participation needs agreement and changes to company law.

subfiles.title: Response on ministerial control of labor affairs
subfiles.about: Tokyo reports on plans for a Japanese Labor Ministry and the proposed transfer of labor functions.
subfiles.summary: Reports that SCAP rejected moving labor functions to the Home Ministry and expects a Labor Ministry in due course.

subfiles.title: SCAP’s Report on Implementation of SWNCC 92
subfiles.about: Sullivan forwards and comments on a SCAP report on Japanese workers’ organizations.
subfiles.summary: Finds substantial implementation of the labor directive and suggests publicizing it amid Soviet criticism.

subfiles.title: Moscow press criticism of Atcheson
subfiles.about: The telegram reports Soviet press coverage of American criticism of Atcheson’s labor policy.
subfiles.summary: Reports Moscow coverage of New York Post and Chicago Sun criticism of Atcheson.

subfiles.title: Functions and Responsibilities of Japanese Police in Labor Disputes
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards instructions on Japanese police conduct during labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SCAP’s memorandum and three translated Home Ministry instructions.

subfiles.title: Instructions of Home Ministry Concerning Functions of Police in Labor Disputes
subfiles.about: SCAP circulates three Japanese Home Ministry instructions concerning police and labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: Lists the November, February, and June translated instructions for labor officers.

subfiles.title: Control of Illegal Actions Accompanying Mass Movements
subfiles.from: Director of the Home Ministry Police Bureau
subfiles.about: The circular explains police control of unlawful conduct at mass gatherings.
subfiles.summary: It instructs police to preserve order without suppressing lawful speech, assembly, or political activity, and clarifies when officers should intervene.

subfiles.title: Prevention and Control of Illegal Actions Accompanying Labor Disputes
subfiles.from: Director of the Home Ministry Police Bureau
subfiles.to: Governors of provinces, municipalities, and prefectures
subfiles.about: The circular limits police action to unlawful conduct connected with labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: It distinguishes labor disputes from accompanying crimes and urges judgment about the seriousness of offenses. Police should avoid obstructing lawful bargaining and should coordinate with prosecutors when judicial action is needed.

subfiles.title: Paying Special Care to Policemen’s Attitude Toward Labor Disputes and the Movement of Laborers
subfiles.from: Director of the Home Ministry Police Bureau
subfiles.to: Metropolitan Police superintendent and prefectural governors
subfiles.about: The circular instructs police to remain impartial and respect union activity.
subfiles.summary: Police are told to stop routine attendance at union meetings, avoid gathering union information, and intervene only for public order or specific crimes.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of the Labor Relations Adjustment Law
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards an English translation of the new Japanese labor law.
subfiles.summary: Highlights dispute procedures and restrictions on certain strikes.

subfiles.title: The Labor Relations Adjustment Law
subfiles.about: The law establishes procedures and limits for resolving labor disputes.
subfiles.summary: The statute defines labor disputes and public welfare work and establishes conciliation, mediation, and arbitration procedures. It restricts actions affecting workplace safety, requires a waiting period for disputes in essential services, and bars certain public employees from dispute actions. It also protects workers against retaliation for lawful dispute activity.

subfiles.title: Recommendations on occupation labor administration
subfiles.about: Schwellenbach urges implementation of the Advisory Committee on Labor’s principal recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Calls for a separate SCAP Labor Section and an independent Japanese Ministry of Labor with cabinet status.

subfiles.title: Final Report of the Advisory Committee on Labor
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards the committee’s July 29 report on labor policy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes that its first chapter condenses the report’s recommendations.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram record
subfiles.to: Department of State, Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: A stamped incoming-airgram page records receipt and filing information.
subfiles.summary: Only receipt stamps and filing marks are legible.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of a Report Concerning Japan’s Labor Movement
subfiles.from: Counselor of Mission, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a SCAP analysis of Japanese publications about labor.
subfiles.summary: Forwards five copies of the April 2 report.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Labor Movement
subfiles.from: SCAP Civil Information and Education Section, Analysis and Research Division
subfiles.about: The report surveys Japanese magazine and newspaper writing on labor issues.
subfiles.summary: These pages review arguments about union growth, political strikes, industrial recovery, and unification of rival labor federations. They compare accounts of electric, newspaper, and railway disputes and summarize debates over wages, prices, and unemployment. The report continues into methods for achieving labor goals at the end of this section.
